clue.text: A book of rates

definitions.meaning: one of the books of the Old Testament, following Joshua
to rate is to assess or evaluate, a verb in the third person

explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament book telling of Israel's leaders; and rating something means assessing its worth, as a critic or referee does.

clue.text: Linbury Court boy's chance to bat with the opener switching to French

definitions.note: the definition carries a possessive; the hero's name stands for the boy

indicators.text: with the opener switching to French
indicators.note: the first letter, the English pronoun I, is swapped for its French equivalent, je

parts.note: a cricket side's turn at batting is its innings

explanation.surface: A schoolboy at Linbury Court gets a turn at the crease, with the opening batsman replaced by a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Linbury Court is the prep school in Anthony Buckeridge's children's books. An innings is a turn to bat in cricket; its opening I becomes French JE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Buckeridge's schoolboy hero attends Linbury Court preparatory school in a long series of comic novels.

clue.text: Judicial enforcer's worry about being overheard

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for 'is', a link, so the definition is the name

indicators.note: something overheard is heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to worry about something is to dread it

explanation.surface: A judge's worry about his words being eavesdropped on.
explanation.definitionFit: Judge Dredd, the comic-strip lawman of 2000 AD, is judge, jury and executioner in one.

clue.text: Brussels stone expert whose diamonds Lizzie kept hold of

definitions.text: whose diamonds Lizzie kept hold of

parts.note: the European Union, headquartered in Brussels, is EU
ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British unit of weight
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A gem specialist from Brussels connected with diamonds that Lizzie refused to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: In Trollope's The Eustace Diamonds, Lizzie, widow of Sir Florian, clings to the family necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel is named for the family whose heirloom necklace the widowed Lizzie insists is hers.

clue.text: Places in our hearts for publishers

definitions.meaning: the heart's four cavities, two atria and two ventricles
the Edinburgh firm known for its dictionary

explanation.definitionFit: The heart has four hollow compartments; and the Scottish publishing house behind a famous dictionary bears this surname.

clue.text: Cheerful nurses raving about Seneca's play

indicators.note: wild raving jumbles the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Happy nurses are ranting about a Roman tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raving' scrambles CHEERFUL and NURSES together. The play's title means 'Hercules mad', which neatly suits the raving.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca's Latin tragedy shows the hero driven insane by Juno, killing his own family.

clue.text: African state with a chapter in a book

indicators.note: the article and chapter go in, placed within the country's name

parts.note: Mali is a state in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African country featuring as a chapter in some volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a book' looks like the start of wordplay, but it is the definition: one of the twelve minor prophets' books.
explanation.definitionFit: The last of the Old Testament's twelve minor prophets gives his name to a short book of the Bible.

clue.text: Having nothing to do with a graphic artist with no right arm

indicators.note: the artist is taken with no trace of the following letter, which is removed

parts.note: M. C. Escher, the Dutch graphic artist of impossible staircases
a wing is an arm of a building or of an organisation

explanation.surface: Avoiding a printmaker who has lost his right arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops the R from ESCHER, leaving ESCHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to shun or abstain from, so the participle means avoiding.

clue.text: Small hill where Kipling placed Puck's spirits

parts.note: Kipling's Puck of Pook's Hill names the Sussex hill

explanation.surface: A little hill where Kipling set his tale of the fairy Puck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghosts and phantoms are informally called spooks, just as the supernatural Puck is a sprite.

clue.text: Brutus, say, about to turn up in neat film genre

parts.note: Brutus is an example of an ancient Roman

indicators.note: the following pieces go in, set within the word for neat

parts.note: tidy means neat
C is short for circa, about
to come is to arrive or turn up

explanation.surface: Brutus about to appear in a well-kept film category.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' makes TICCOMEDY. 'neat' is easily read as undiluted (a neat drink) or as cattle; here it means tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of cinema about love affairs played for laughs, the rom-com.

clue.text: Nobel and his odd run as a scientist

indicators.note: the letters are set in an odd, unusual arrangement

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Alfred Nobel and his strange spell, presented as a scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges NOBEL and HIS into NIELSBOH; R closes it. Fittingly, the answer won a Nobel Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish physicist modelled the atom and won the 1922 Nobel Prize for physics.

clue.text: Claudio's friend uncovered much in painting from the east

indicators.note: the middle letters are placed in the other word
in an across entry, reading from the east means right to left, so the word for painting is turned round

parts.note: oil is a painting done in oils

indicators.note: with its cover taken off, only the middle of the word much remains

explanation.surface: A friend of Claudio removed much of the covering in a picture from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns the painting word to LIO. In Measure for Measure, Lucio pleads Claudio's case to Isabella.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Measure for Measure the fantastic gadabout urges Isabella to plead for her brother Claudio's life.

clue.text: God overwhelmed by blind rage

indicators.note: the answer is submerged by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A deity swamped by a fit of uncontrolled fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vedic king of the gods wields thunder and lightning in Hindu mythology.

clue.text: Fit half of Bottom's part in Twelfth Night

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever and shivering
a bottom has two buttocks, so one of them is half of it

explanation.surface: A turn of fever and half of Bottom's role in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, which tempts a solver to think of roles; here it is just the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Andrew, the foolish knight who courts Olivia in Shakespeare's comedy, is a character in the play.

clue.text: Persuaded to accept medal by king, he's tricked by 'the two clerks'

indicators.note: the first word takes the others in, holding them inside

parts.note: got, as in got someone to do something, means persuaded
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone coaxed into accepting an honour from the king is taken in by a pair of clerks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to accept' does the containing. Gombert is the host gulled by two young clerks in La Fontaine's tale, a reworking of Chaucer's Reeve's Tale story.
explanation.definitionFit: In La Fontaine's verse tale the householder whose wife and daughter are seduced by two visiting clerks is named Gombert.

clue.text: Email when off work, from H. G. Wells

indicators.note: off means not right, so the letters are set wrongly in a new order

explanation.surface: Sending an email while away from work, as H. G. Wells might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges EMAIL and WHEN. 'work' looks like part of 'off work' but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wells published a 1927 novel of this title, subtitled The Picture of a Lady.

clue.text: lago's wife's excellent fruit turnover

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition names the wife

indicators.note: turning over the pair reverses the whole run of letters

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Iago's wife makes a superb fruit pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' reverses AILIME as one block. A turnover is also a fruit pastry, which is the surface's disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Othello, Iago is married to Desdemona's attendant, who finally exposes his plot.

clue.text: "I am by birth a —— " (Victor Frankenstein)

definitions.text: I am by birth a —— " (Victor Frankenstein

parts.words: I am by birth a —— " (Victor Frankenstein
parts.note: a quotation with a blank: the opening words of Victor's own account of his birth in Mary Shelley's novel

explanation.walkthrough: Victor Frankenstein begins his narrative by giving his nationality as a native of Geneva.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Geneva, as Victor tells Walton at the start of his story in Shelley's novel.

clue.text: Like a sonnet's line two about a doctor, hapless chap

indicators.note: the numeral goes about the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor
read as 'hap-less chap': chap with HAP removed leaves C

explanation.surface: Describing a sonnet's second line about a medic, an unlucky fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does the containing. 'hapless' splits as 'hap less', taking HAP from CHAP to leave C.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets in English are usually written in iambic pentameter, lines of five unstressed-stressed feet.

clue.text: A biographer shed tears over spring

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry, shedding tears
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: A biographer wept over a water source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SOB to BOS.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the celebrated Life of Samuel Johnson, the model of English biography.

clue.text: Fellow regularly battling Auden's languor

indicators.note: taken regularly, every other letter is picked

explanation.surface: A man persistently struggling against the poet Auden's lethargy.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and so on letters of 'battling Auden' give ATIGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is weariness or lack of energy, the same as exhaustion.

clue.text: Anna Seghers's work of art isn't bad

indicators.note: bad as in wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A German novelist's work of art is not bad at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges ART and ISNT; the apostrophe is not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Seghers wrote her 1944 novel about refugees in Marseille waiting for visas under this title.

clue.text: I must enter a highland town to oust second rival of Valentine

indicators.note: the letter I has to go into the town's name in place of another
it goes in to push out a letter, which is lost

parts.note: Thurso is a town on the north coast of the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: I have to move into a Scottish town to displace a rival in love.
explanation.walkthrough: THURSO is the northernmost town on the British mainland. Its S is replaced by I.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Two Gentlemen of Verona, the foolish suitor favoured by Silvia's father competes with Valentine for her.

clue.text: Attempts to sell second or third Ackroyd novel

parts.note: to hawk goods is to peddle them
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A seller tries to shift a few seconds or so of an Ackroyd book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second or third' looks like one phrase, but 'second' gives MO, 'or' stands as it is, and 'third' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Ackroyd's 1985 novel about a church architect and a modern detective followed two earlier fictions.

clue.text: A barrier for a critic and diarist

parts.note: a gate is a barrier in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A fence across the way for a reviewer who keeps a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: James Agate was the Sunday Times drama critic whose multivolume diaries were published as Ego.

clue.text: Party-goer, one with cold beer bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the beer encloses the others

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A partygoer drinks with someone holding bottled cold beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' puts I and C inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroll's heroine attends the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Martian poet's rule for listeners

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', a link, so the definition names the poet

indicators.note: said for those listening, the word counts by how it sounds

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: A poet from Mars lays down a principle for his audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Craig Raine led the 'Martian' school of poetry, after his poem A Martian Sends a Postcard Home.
explanation.definitionFit: Craig Raine's poem A Martian Sends a Postcard Home gave its name to the Martian school of poets.

clue.text: Cosy place in Ireland beginning to enjoy Laclos's comic opera

indicators.note: the cosy place sits in the name for Ireland

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland
a nest is a snug, cosy place

indicators.note: only the beginning of the word, its first letter, is used

explanation.surface: A snug spot in Ireland, the start of enjoying a French author's opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Choderlos de Laclos wrote the libretto of this 1777 opéra comique; 'Cosy place' reads like a description of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Laclos, author of Les Liaisons dangereuses, wrote the libretto of a comic opera with music by Saint-Georges.

clue.text: Covers of songs done before

indicators.note: the word for done comes before the songs in the answer

parts.note: over means finished, done
lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: Cover versions of songs that have already been recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers of songs' suggests music, but Covers is a noun meaning layers on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlays are coverings laid over a surface, such as a transparent sheet over a map.
